original_value: Barrier coverage has been widely used to detect intrusions in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). It can fulfill the monitoring task while extending the lifetime of the network. Though barrier coverage in WSNs has been intensively studied in recent years, previous research failed to consider the problem of intrusion in transversal directions. If an intruder knows the deployment configuration of sensor nodes, then there is a high probability that it may traverse the whole target region from particular directions, without being detected. In this paper, we introduce the concept of crossed barrier coverage that can overcome this defect. We prove that the problem of finding the maximum number of crossed barriers is NP-hard and integer linear programming (ILP) is used to formulate the optimization problem. The branch-and-bound algorithm is adopted to determine the maximum number of crossed barriers. In addition, we also propose a multi-round shortest path algorithm (MSPA) to solve the optimization problem, which works heuristically to guarantee efficiency while maintaining near-optimal solutions. Several conventional algorithms for finding the maximum number of disjoint strong barriers are also modified to solve the crossed barrier problem and for the purpose of comparison. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of MSPA.

result.paraphrase: Barrier coverage has been widely adopted for intrusion detection in wireless sensor networks (WSNs), as it can accomplish monitoring tasks while prolonging network lifetime. Although barrier coverage in WSNs has been studied extensively in recent years, earlier work did not address intrusion from transversal directions. If an intruder is aware of the sensor-node deployment pattern, it may have a high chance of crossing the entire target area from certain directions without detection. To address this limitation, this paper introduces crossed barrier coverage. We show that finding the maximum number of crossed barriers is NP-hard, and model the optimization problem using integer linear programming (ILP). The branch-and-bound algorithm is employed to compute the maximum number of crossed barriers. We also present a multi-round shortest path algorithm (MSPA) as a heuristic solution that ensures efficiency while producing near-optimal results. In addition, several standard algorithms for finding the maximum number of disjoint strong barriers are adapted for the crossed barrier problem and used for comparison. Extensive simulation results show that MSPA is effective.
